no mls qos

stem: Why is voice normally kept in its own VLAN, separate from the data VLAN that serves the PCs?
explanation: A dedicated voice VLAN lets the network apply a QoS policy, a security policy, and a DHCP scope to phones alone, and it keeps PC broadcast traffic away from latency-sensitive call signalling. A phone sharing the data VLAN cannot be given different treatment without also treating the PCs that way.

choices.text: So QoS, security policy, and the DHCP scope can target phone traffic independently of PC traffic
Because a phone cannot tag frames unless it is in a separate VLAN
Because voice VLANs bypass spanning tree to reduce latency
Because trunking requires at least two VLANs on every port

stem: A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not present in its MAC address table. What does it do with the frame?
explanation: An unknown destination cannot be mapped to a port, so the switch floods the frame out every other port in the same VLAN. That flooding is exactly what a MAC flooding attack exploits, filling the table with bogus entries so legitimate destinations also look unknown.

choices.text: Floods it out of every other port in the same VLAN
Drops it and sends an ICMP unreachable message
Sends it only to the default gateway port
Holds it until the destination sends a frame and is learned

stem: Which command lists the MAC addresses a switch has learned, along with their VLANs and ports?
explanation: show mac address-table prints the CAM contents with VLAN, type, and port so you can confirm whether a host was learned on the expected access port. It is the first check when a host is reachable from some parts of the network but not others.

choices.text: show mac address-table
show arp
show interface status
show vlan brief

stem: Which statement is true of a MAC address entry created with the mac address-table static command?
explanation: Static entries are administrative and are never aged out, unlike dynamically learned ones that disappear after the aging time or a reload. That permanence is useful for pinned server ports, but it also means a stale static entry survives until someone removes it.

choices.text: It is never aged out and remains until it is removed manually
It ages out after 300 seconds like a dynamic entry
It is cleared whenever the switch is reloaded
It can only be created on a trunk port

stem: A single MAC address keeps appearing on two different switch ports within seconds of each other. What does this most likely indicate?
explanation: The switch follows the source address of the newest frame, so the entry bounces between ports as frames arrive from both directions. That flapping is the classic signature of a Layer 2 loop, or of a duplicated MAC such as a cloned VM or a misconfigured NIC team.

choices.text: A Layer 2 loop or a duplicated MAC address
Normal ageing behaviour of dynamic entries
The switch running out of CAM table space
A mismatch between the native VLANs on a trunk

stem: Which command enables storm control for broadcast traffic at 20 percent of the interface bandwidth?
explanation: The level keyword takes a percentage of the interface's total bandwidth when no unit is given, and each traffic type is configured separately. Broadcast, multicast, and unknown unicast therefore need three separate statements if all three should be limited.

choices.text: storm-control broadcast level 20
storm-control broadcast 20 mbps
storm-control level broadcast 20
switchport storm-control broadcast 20

stem: Which storm-control action keyword takes the port out of service when the configured threshold is exceeded?
explanation: The shutdown keyword err-disables the interface, which stops the storm but also drops every legitimate frame on that port. The trap keyword only reports the condition, and plain storm control with no action simply discards the excess traffic while the port stays up.

choices.text: shutdown
trap
restrict
protect

stem: Storm control with the shutdown action placed a port in the err-disabled state. What restores it?
explanation: An err-disabled port has to be cycled with shutdown and no shutdown, or recovered automatically if errdisable recovery has been enabled for the storm-control cause. Either way the underlying storm has to be resolved first, or the port will simply be disabled again.

choices.text: Issue shutdown then no shutdown, or enable errdisable recovery for the storm-control cause
Clear the MAC address table
Reload the switch
Remove the storm-control command from the interface

stem: Which storm-control syntax limits broadcast traffic to a packet rate rather than a percentage of bandwidth?
explanation: Adding the pps keyword switches the threshold from a percentage of the interface bandwidth to packets per second, which is far more predictable on links whose speed is not fixed. A percentage on a 10 Gbps port allows an enormous packet rate that may still overwhelm a slow attached device.

choices.text: storm-control broadcast level pps 500
storm-control broadcast rate 500 pps
storm-control broadcast packets 500
storm-control broadcast level 500 bps

stem: What are the default CDP advertisement interval and hold time on a Cisco device?
explanation: CDP sends an advertisement every 60 seconds and tells the neighbour to keep the entry for 180 seconds, so three advertisements can be lost before the neighbour is removed. Both values can be changed with the cdp timer and cdp holdtime commands.

choices.text: 60 seconds interval, 180 seconds hold time
30 seconds interval, 120 seconds hold time
120 seconds interval, 360 seconds hold time
10 seconds interval, 30 seconds hold time

stem: Which interface command stops CDP from advertising on a single port while leaving CDP running globally?
explanation: no cdp enable disables CDP on that one interface, which is what a hardening baseline does on ports facing an untrusted network. The global no cdp run would disable the protocol everywhere and break neighbour discovery on every other link.

choices.text: no cdp enable
no cdp run
no cdp advertise-v2
cdp disable

stem: Which command shows a CDP neighbour's platform, software version, and management address rather than just its name and port?
explanation: show cdp neighbors prints one line per neighbour with the local port and the neighbour's port, while the detail keyword adds the platform, IOS version, and address list. Those extra fields are what let you verify a device's software release remotely.

choices.text: show cdp neighbors detail
show cdp neighbors
show cdp interface
show cdp traffic

stem: Which two interface commands control whether a port sends and accepts LLDP advertisements?
explanation: LLDP is enabled globally with lldp run and then tuned per interface with lldp transmit and lldp receive separately. That split is useful on an edge port where you want to receive neighbour data but not advertise the switch's own identity, or the reverse.

choices.text: lldp transmit and lldp receive
lldp run and no lldp run
lldp enable and lldp disable
lldp advertise and lldp listen

stem: What does 802.11r fast BSS transition change about a client roaming between access points?
explanation: A normal roam repeats the full authentication and key exchange at the new AP, which is slow enough to break a voice call. 802.11r pre-establishes the security keys across the mobility domain so the client can resume at the new AP with a short handshake instead of a full one.

choices.text: It pre-establishes keys so the client can rekey quickly at the new access point
It gives the client a list of neighbour access points to consider
It encrypts management frames to prevent deauthentication attacks
It lets the client keep its IP address across different subnets

stem: Several clients use an SSID successfully, but one laptop can see the SSID and still fails to join. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: An SSID that broadcasts correctly but rejects one specific client usually means a policy the client cannot satisfy, such as a WPA3-only WLAN when the adapter only supports WPA2, or a protected management frames requirement the driver does not implement. The radio link is working, so the failure happens at the security stage.

choices.text: The client does not support the security policy the WLAN requires, such as WPA3 or protected management frames
The SSID is hidden from that client only
The client is out of range of every access point
The DHCP scope for the WLAN is exhausted

stem: A wireless client joins the correct SSID and gets an address, but it lands in the wrong VLAN. Where is the mapping defined?
explanation: The controller decides which VLAN a wireless client belongs to by mapping the WLAN to an interface or VLAN, and the frame is then tagged onto the trunk toward the access switch. A client in the wrong subnet is therefore a mapping mistake on the controller, not a problem with the client or the AP.

choices.text: In the WLAN-to-interface mapping on the wireless controller
In the client's own IP configuration
In the access point's radio profile
In the DHCP scope on the client's subnet

stem: What does client exclusion do on a wireless controller?
explanation: Client exclusion blocks a specific MAC address for a configured period after repeated authentication or association failures. It limits the damage from a client stuck in a failing retry loop, but it also means a misconfigured device stays off the network even after the configuration is corrected until the timer expires.

choices.text: It blocks a client's MAC address for a period after repeated failures
It removes the client from the controller's mobility group
It permanently denies every client that misses a DHCP request
It disables the SSID the client was trying to join

stem: Which pair of commands defines a local SPAN session that copies traffic from Gi0/1 to Gi0/2?
explanation: A SPAN session always needs both a source and a destination statement under the same session number. The source can be an interface or a VLAN, and the destination is the port where the analyzer is plugged in.

choices.text: monitor session 1 source interface Gi0/1, then monitor session 1 destination interface Gi0/2
span source Gi0/1, then span destination Gi0/2
monitor capture Gi0/1 both, then monitor export Gi0/2
interface Gi0/1 monitor, then interface Gi0/2 mirror

stem: How does a port behave while it is the destination of a SPAN session?
explanation: A SPAN destination port gives up its normal switching role and transmits only the mirrored copies, so it neither forwards user traffic nor learns addresses. Attaching a device that answers on that port can disturb the capture, which is why analyzers usually just listen.

choices.text: It stops forwarding normal user traffic and only transmits the mirrored copies
It forwards user traffic and mirrored copies at the same time by default
It becomes a trunk carrying the mirrored VLAN
It shuts down until the session is removed

stem: What does a SPAN session capture when its source is configured as a VLAN instead of an interface?
explanation: A VLAN source mirrors traffic on every port that belongs to that VLAN, including frames switched between two local hosts that never leave the switch. That makes it useful for capturing a whole segment, at the cost of far more traffic than a single port would generate.

choices.text: Traffic on every port in that VLAN, including frames switched locally between hosts
Only traffic that leaves the switch toward the default gateway
Only broadcast and multicast frames in that VLAN
Only frames arriving on the trunk ports carrying that VLAN

stem: Which VLAN-level command must be applied to the VLAN that carries mirrored frames in an RSPAN session?
explanation: An RSPAN VLAN has to be declared with remote-span so the switches treat it as a transport for mirrored traffic rather than a normal VLAN. Without it the mirrored frames are flooded normally and the session never delivers a clean capture to the destination switch.

choices.text: remote-span, entered in VLAN configuration mode
monitor session 1 remote vlan
spanning-tree portfast, entered on every port in the VLAN
vlan dot1q tag native on each trunk

stem: Two virtual machines on the same hypervisor and the same port group exchange frames. Does that traffic reach the physical network?
explanation: The virtual switch forwards between vNICs in software, so the frames are delivered without ever touching an uplink. That is why a capture taken on the physical switch sees nothing for this traffic and the analyzer has to run inside the hypervisor instead.

choices.text: No; the virtual switch forwards the frames internally in software
Yes; every frame is sent to the physical switch first
Only if the two virtual machines are in different VLANs
Only if promiscuous mode is enabled on the port group

stem: What does NIC teaming provide when several physical adapters are attached to one virtual switch?
explanation: Teaming bonds multiple physical NICs into one logical uplink, so a failed adapter does not take the host off the network and the aggregate bandwidth exceeds that of a single link. The exact load-balancing behaviour depends on the policy chosen and on how the physical switch is configured.

choices.text: Redundancy if an adapter fails and more bandwidth than one link alone
A separate VLAN for each virtual machine automatically
Encryption of all traffic leaving the host
A guarantee that each virtual machine uses a dedicated physical NIC

stem: Which port group security policy stops a virtual machine from presenting a MAC address that was never assigned to it?
explanation: The MAC address changes policy governs frames received from the guest, and forged transmits covers frames the guest sends with a source MAC it does not own. Rejecting both closes the spoofing hole that otherwise lets one virtual machine impersonate another on the same segment.

choices.text: MAC address changes, together with forged transmits
Promiscuous mode
Traffic shaping
The uplink teaming policy

stem: How is a virtual machine's traffic placed into a specific VLAN on a standard virtual switch?
explanation: The port group carries the VLAN ID and the virtual switch tags frames as they leave toward the uplink, so the guest itself stays VLAN-unaware. The alternative is to give the guest a trunk and let it tag its own frames, which requires the port group to allow VLAN 4095.

choices.text: The port group holds the VLAN ID and the virtual switch tags the frames
The guest operating system must tag its own frames in every case
The physical switch detects the guest and assigns a VLAN dynamically
Each virtual machine is bound to a dedicated uplink in that VLAN

stem: Which legacy Cisco feature gives an access switch an immediate alternate path when its root port fails?
explanation: UplinkFast keeps a secondary uplink ready and moves it straight to forwarding when the root port goes down, instead of waiting through the 802.1D listening and learning timers. It also limits how much the switch can disturb the topology, which is why it is meant only for access-layer switches.

choices.text: UplinkFast
Root Guard
Loop Guard
BPDU Guard

stem: What does BPDU Filter do when it is applied to a PortFast interface?
explanation: BPDU Filter stops the port from sending BPDUs and ignores any it receives, which effectively removes the port from spanning tree. That is safe only toward an end host; accidentally applying it toward another switch creates exactly the loop spanning tree exists to prevent.

choices.text: It stops sending BPDUs and ignores received BPDUs, effectively removing the port from spanning tree
It places the port in the root-inconsistent state when a superior BPDU arrives
It converts the port into a designated port regardless of topology
It slows the port's transition to forwarding to detect loops

stem: Which command makes a switch automatically re-enable ports that BPDU Guard has err-disabled?
explanation: errdisable recovery cause bpduguard enables automatic recovery, and the interval is set separately, defaulting to 300 seconds. Without it, every BPDU Guard violation needs a manual shutdown and no shutdown on the port.

choices.text: errdisable recovery cause bpduguard
spanning-tree bpduguard enable recovery
no spanning-tree bpduguard default
errdisable detect cause bpduguard

stem: Which three port states exist in Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (802.1w)?
explanation: RSTP folded the 802.1D disabled, blocking, and listening states into a single discarding state, leaving discarding, learning, and forwarding. Fewer states mean a port can move directly from discarding to forwarding once the proposal and agreement exchange succeeds.

choices.text: Discarding, learning, and forwarding
Blocking, listening, and forwarding
Disabled, blocking, and learning
Discarding, listening, and forwarding

stem: How does an RSTP edge port behave when a cable is plugged into it?
explanation: An edge port assumes an end host is attached, so it moves straight to forwarding without the proposal and agreement exchange and without generating a topology change. It is the RSTP equivalent of PortFast, and the same caution applies: connecting another switch to it invites a loop.

choices.text: It moves directly to forwarding and does not trigger a topology change
It waits for the proposal and agreement handshake before forwarding
It becomes the root port for the segment
It stays in discarding until a BPDU is received

stem: How quickly does RSTP conclude that a neighbour on a point-to-point link has failed?
explanation: RSTP treats the loss of three consecutive hellos as a failure, which at the default two-second hello interval is about six seconds. That is far faster than 802.1D, which waits out the full max-age timer before even beginning to reconverge.

choices.text: After three missed hellos, roughly six seconds at the default interval
After the 20-second max-age timer expires
After 30 seconds of listening and learning
Only when the interface line protocol goes down

stem: Which interface command disables Power over Ethernet delivery on a switch port?
explanation: power inline never stops the port from detecting and powering a device, which is what you want on a port that should only ever serve a non-PoE host. It is a per-port setting, so the rest of the switch keeps powering phones and access points normally.

choices.text: power inline never
no power inline
power inline off
poe disable

stem: Which mechanism does 802.3at use beyond hardware classification to negotiate power above the 15.4 W class limit?
explanation: Hardware classification only carries a few power classes, so 802.3at adds LLDP-based negotiation that lets the powered device and the PSE agree on a higher figure. That is how a PoE+ access point can request 25 W rather than being capped at the class ceiling.

choices.text: LLDP power negotiation between the powered device and the PSE
A second round of resistance detection at a higher voltage
CDP advertisements carrying a wattage field
DHCP option 82 in the device's address request

stem: A powered device draws more current than the PSE allocated to its port. What does the PSE do?
explanation: The PSE monitors the port and removes power when the device exceeds its allocation, which protects the switch's power supply and the cabling. The port then has to go through detection again before power is restored, so an undersized allocation looks like a device that keeps rebooting.

choices.text: It removes power from the port and the device must be detected again
It delivers the extra power and logs a warning
It drops the port's data traffic but keeps power applied
It moves the device to a higher power class automatically

stem: What is the default port security violation mode on a Cisco switch?
explanation: The default is shutdown, which err-disables the port on the first violation and raises a syslog message. Because that takes the port out of service, many access designs deliberately change it to restrict so a single unauthorised device does not silence a working port.

choices.text: shutdown
restrict
protect
trap

stem: Which links carry VTP advertisements between switches?
explanation: VTP advertisements are sent only over trunk links, so a switch reachable solely through access ports never learns the domain's VLAN database. That is why a new switch cabled to an access port can sit in the domain with a stale database and no error.

choices.text: Trunk links only
Any link between two switches, access or trunk
Only links configured as EtherChannel members
Only routed links between Layer 3 switches
